--- title: "Speech perception: identification II" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA_II" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA_II`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Percepción del habla: identificación II*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA_II.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Speech perception: identification II, at age 4 (384 administrations in 1 cohorts). AUC .63 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2026 | | Battery | — | | Format | auditory stimuli | | Items | — | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | INSTRUCCIONES Tenemos un amigo extraterrestre que está aprendiendo a hablar nuestro idioma. Al pobre le está costando muchísimo y sólo puede decir la primera sílaba (trocito) de cada palabra. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework The **categorical perception** tasks (Serniclaes battery) use synthetic syllables ranging from BA to PA in voicing steps. In identification, the child says which syllable they hear; in discrimination, whether two syllables are the same or different. **Minimal pairs** ask the child to decide whether two real syllables are the same or different. They measure the precision of phonemic categories, the basis of letter–sound correspondences. **Phonological fluency** (saying, in 30 seconds, words that begin with a given phoneme) measures something else: lexical access from a sound and executive control. **What the evidence says:** - **Dyslexia shows a categorical perception deficit, clearer in discrimination.** A meta-analysis confirms the deficit compared with children of the same age and with younger readers at the same level. The effect is larger in discrimination than in identification [@noordenbos2015meta]. - **In Spanish, what fails is the boundary between categories.** In 204 Spanish children, those with dyslexia discriminated pairs that cross the phonemic boundary worse and some within-category differences better (allophonic perception) [@serniclaes2021allophonic]. That is why the total of correct responses mixes two effects of opposite sign. - **Its predictive value is modest and not entirely phonological.** In 237 children, perception at age 5½ predicted reading a year later without going through phonemic awareness. These tasks also capture decision making [@snowling2019speech]. In another study, its effect on decoding disappeared when phonological processing was controlled [@mcbridechang1997growth]. The evidence is therefore contradictory. - **Phonological fluency reflects access, not representations.** In 66 Greek children with dyslexia or developmental language disorder, word production was lower, but the size of clusters of related words was the same as in 83 controls [@mengisidou2019fluency]. **What our data show.** - **Categorical perception.** Discrimination does not predict persistent difficulty (AUC .39–.53) and identification barely does (.51–.63). This is to be expected if the total of correct responses is scored: the identification slope and between- and within-category discrimination should be computed from the item-by-item responses. - **Minimal pairs.** Low stability (ρ = .07–.39) and AUC from .45 to .69, better from age 5. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, .63–.66 at ages 6–7. - **Phonological fluency.** A single session at age 5 (793 children, almost all from Preleo schools): AUC of .68 against persistent difficulty and of .59–.62 against low comprehension. It is related to phonological awareness, letters and reading (ρ = .41–.43). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.3| 2012| 158|2016/17 | 384| 380| 0| 17| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.3| 380| 2012| 11.68| 5.41| 11| -0.12| 5.26| 15.53| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 4.3| 380|0–20 |0–20 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Rapid naming (RAN) (4.3, r = .12). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .63. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA_II_F2_validez.png){width=85%} ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.3| 380| 2012| 0| 5| 8| 9| 11| 16| 20| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA_II_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.3| 268| -0.024| 0.700| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.3| 384| 0.252| 0.014| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.3| 380| 0.035| 0.496| |School (ICC) | 4.3| 384| 0.180| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Speech perception: identification II” (code 2026) assesses speech perception. Stimuli are presented auditorily and the child responds by selecting on the screen. The time limit is 180 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2012 cohorts it was administered in 1 session, from 4 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 4.3 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
